title: Authorising an external signer over Grove's Ethena orders requires only the relayer role and is subject to no rate limit
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.10.1 defines `setDelegatedSigner` as "authorizing a signer to sign Ethena mint and redeem orders on behalf of the Grove ALM Proxy", and A...10.1.2 shows the whole implementation: a `_checkRole(RELAYER)` followed by `proxy.doCall(ethenaMinter, setDelegatedSigner(delegatedSigner))`. A...10.2 mirrors it for revocation.

Compare this to the neighbouring functions. `prepareUSDeMint`, `prepareUSDeBurn` and `cooldownAssetsSUSDe` all pass through `_rateLimited(...)` before acting. The delegation functions do not, because there is no amount to meter — but that is precisely what makes them the highest-leverage calls in the module. A rate limit bounds how much value a compromised relayer can move per period; delegation instead **transfers the capability itself** to an address of the relayer's choosing, outside any amount-based control.

The tension is structural rather than a bug: Grove's safety model is two-layered (role plus quantitative limit, per A...7.2.1 and the `_rateLimited` calls throughout), and this is the one place where the second layer is inapplicable, leaving the relayer key as the sole control.

The mitigation available is that `removeDelegatedSigner` exists and is equally cheap, so revocation is always one relayer transaction away — which shifts the burden onto monitoring for unexpected delegations rather than preventing them.
description: setDelegatedSigner and removeDelegatedSigner are the only Ethena operations with no _rateLimited call, yet they hand a third party the power to sign mint and redeem orders for the proxy.
